title: Django Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Make a text view
examples.description: A view is a function that returns a response. path connects the empty path to hello. Open GET /.

examples.title: Send named data
examples.description: JsonResponse turns a Python dictionary into JSON. Open GET /book/.

examples.title: Read a checked path number
examples.description: The int converter turns a matching path part into a Python int. Open GET /double/4/.

examples.title: Read a name from the path
examples.description: The str converter passes one path segment as text. Open GET /hello/Ravi/.

examples.title: Read a query string
examples.description: request.GET contains query values. Visit GET /search/?q=cat.

examples.title: Allow only a chosen method
examples.description: A view can inspect request.method. A GET request to /check/ is accepted; another method gets 405.

examples.title: Build a URL from its name
examples.description: reverse finds a route by name and fills its inputs. Open GET /link/.

examples.title: Send a client elsewhere
examples.description: redirect creates an HTTP redirect. GET /start/ sends a browser to /hello/.

examples.title: Return an error status
examples.description: The response status describes the result. Open GET /missing/ to see a 404 reply.

examples.title: Return a list safely
examples.description: JsonResponse normally expects a dictionary. A dictionary can hold a list under a clear key. Open GET /books/.

examples.title: Set response metadata
examples.description: A response object can store headers. GET /note/ has a no-store cache rule.
examples.code:
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse, HttpResponseNotAllowed
from django.shortcuts import redirect
from django.urls import path, reverse
import json
def note(request):
    response = HttpResponse("Practice note", content_type="text/plain")
    response["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    return response
urlpatterns = [
path("note/", note),
]

examples.title: Make a small health response
examples.description: A health route gives a small answer that a checker can read. GET /health/ returns one Boolean field.
